scoreSemantics: Nearshore thermal fit is a bounded FinFindr adjustment estimating whether the modeled surface-water temperature is compatible with pier-reachable opportunity. It is not the fish's experienced temperature, a biological rating, fish-presence measurement, or catch probability.
changeSummary: The v0.2 private candidate raises only the sub-50 F cold shoulders. Every v0.1 value at 10 C / 50 F and warmer is retained for an isolated comparison.

curves.limitations: The 10–14 C plateau follows a general agency range; the 9 C anchor reflects method-specific Lake Michigan gillnet catch and is not treated as a pier-bite optimum. The v0.2 cold shoulder is a provisional FinFindr pier-reachability calibration; the v0.1 curve is retained in code for comparison.

The 12–14 C plateau follows a general agency range. The historical 16.6 C adult observation supports a gradual warm shoulder, not a second optimum. The v0.2 cold shoulder is provisional; the warm side is unchanged from v0.1.

The 12–14 C plateau follows a general agency range. The v0.2 cold shoulder is broader so winter and spring pier opportunity is not erased by an unsupported narrow optimum; strain and migration differences are not separately scored. The warm side is unchanged from v0.1.

The 10–16 C plateau and broad 8–18 C high-suitability region reconcile Michigan agency context with Great Lakes adult occupancy. The v0.2 cold shoulder recognizes early-spring pier opportunity; the conflicting Wisconsin 18–24 C range is not used as a universal optimum and the warm side remains unchanged from v0.1.
